steps.title: Sedentary Lifestyle
steps.body: A way of living that involves little or no physical activity, characterised by prolonged periods of sitting or lying down during waking hours. A person with a sedentary lifestyle does not meet the recommended levels of physical activity for health.

steps.title: Obesity
steps.body: A medical condition where a person has excess body fat to the extent that it may have a negative effect on their health. Obesity is commonly defined as having a BMI (Body Mass Index) of 30 or above.

steps.title: PE Exam Tips — Sedentary Lifestyle and Obesity
steps.body: 1. For Sedentary Lifestyle and Obesity questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Sedentary Lifestyle and Obesity to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the BMI formula and categories - you may be asked to calculate and classify Sedentary lifestyle consequences: obesity, CHD, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis, muscle atrophy Always explain HOW inactivity causes each consequence, not just that it does Obesity affects performance: CV endurance, flexibility, speed and injury risk Address physical, mental AND social impacts separately for full marks Remember the "vicious cycle" concept - inactivity leads to problems that cause more inactivity
